node.title: Re^3: Contextual find and replace large config file
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Why (?:\z| ) and not just \z when \z is 'up to and including '

Not quite, \z only ever matches at the very end of the string, whereas \Z also matches before the newline at the end of the string, and the meaning of $ is changed by the /m modifier to match before every newline or at the end of the string. When I want to express "match up to the end of this line", I sometimes prefer (?:\z| ) over $+/m because the former explicitly consumes the .

Why \h* * and not \s*

Because /\s*/ would also match e.g. , which causes a following /^.../ to no longer match, since /\s*/ consumed the at the beginning of the line.

Update: Regarding the first point:

$ perl -MData::Dump -e 'dd split /($)/m, "x y z"' ("x", "", " y", "", " z") $ perl -MData::Dump -e 'dd split /(\z| )/m, "x y z"' ("x", " ", "y", " ", "z")
